timeline.text: Brianna Lewis reports sudden abdominal pain and fetal bradycardia during TOLAC. The nurse notes trial of labor after cesarean and begins focused safety assessment.
The condition progresses with sudden severe abdominal pain between contractions. The nurse stays with the client and escalates monitoring.
Diagnostic data now show Fetal monitor shows prolonged bradycardia with sudden loss of station on exam. The cue pattern supports Uterine rupture with fetal and maternal hemorrhage risk.
Orders are initiated for stop oxytocin if infusing and activate obstetric emergency response. The nurse avoids continue oxytocin to speed delivery because it could delay rescue.
After priority interventions, team moves to emergency surgery. The nurse continues reassessment because fetal compromise remains time-critical.
Final reassessment shows maternal BP supported with fluids/blood readiness. Ongoing concern remains because hemorrhage risk persists.
